speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an adolescent experiencing delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To begin our assessment, have you ever suffered a fracture from a fall that would have been typical of everyday life for someone your age?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency).

I have noted the history of fractures, delayed menarche, and the specific physical features of labial fusion, clitoromegaly, and maternal hirsutism during pregnancy. These findings strongly suggest a disorder of steroidogenesis; I will now request a morning cortisol, 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and electrolyte panel to confirm the diagnosis.
